reading.body:
Zhejiang University holds 1,077 granted US patents, and its most recent five, all granted in September 2026, include power-flow calculation for grid-following systems and a programmable-conducting-current diode array.

The patent record is the substantive signal here. The recent grants cluster around device physics and power electronics: a diode device with programmable conducting current and its array preparation method, a perovskite laser, a liver CT segmentation algorithm, microwave frequency selection, and joint power flow calculation based on grid-following impedance. Two of the five touch power conversion or grid modeling directly, which is the kind of work that sits upstream of data-center electrical infrastructure rather than downstream of AI models.

The profile text describes a broad research university, with items on super-resolution imaging, transition-metal dichalcogenide nanotubes, and vinblastine, plus seminars on decoding Chinese industrial policy with large language models and on social media's effect on firm boundaries. None of that is AI infrastructure work. The record lists no products, no litigation, and no MCP servers.

What this does not establish is any connection between the university and AI compute buildout. The patent count is a measure of institutional research output, not of capacity, procurement, or deployment. The grid-following power flow patent is a modeling method, and the data does not say whether it is licensed, used, or relevant to any specific facility.

profile_text.body:
Zhejiang University is a nonprofit university based in Hangzhou, China, described in the record as a university-lab organization. Its English-language site carries research news and seminar announcements from its schools and departments.

The research items on the site include work on super-resolution imaging that avoids external light excitation by using the faint light generated by chemical reactions, and an international team led by Xiang Rong of the School of Mechanical Engineering that reports the first preferred synthesis of transition-metal dichalcogenide nanotubes. Another item concerns vinblastine, the chemotherapy drug sourced from the Madagascar periwinkle. The site also lists seminars: Li Ming's abstract describes using large language models to decode China's industrial policies from 2000 to 2022 across a dataset of 3.3 million documents issued by central, provincial, and city-level governments; Buhui Qiu's examines whether specialized investment social media shapes firm boundaries by promoting strategic alliances; and Xinyu Cao's looks at whether buyer-generated images in product reviews help or hurt subsequent sales.

The record lists no products, no litigation, and no MCP servers for the university.
